Rationale: Bond-like, defensive sector. Benefits from falling yields. Hurt when rates rise sharply (higher financing costs, unattractive vs bonds).
Relatively defensive: demand is non-discretionary and less cyclical. Provides stable earnings across most macro environments.
Long-duration growth asset: valued on distant future earnings. Very sensitive to changes in discount rates (yields).
Depends on disposable income: employment, real wages, and consumer confidence. Inflation squeezing real wages is the main headwind.
Revenues driven by commodity prices. Inflation and global demand are positives; demand collapse is a key risk.
Driven by manufacturing activity, capex cycles, and trade. PMI and global demand are the key leading indicators.
Benefits from steeper yield curves (higher NIM) and rising rates. Hurt by recession risk and credit deterioration.
